headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure from Flowise’s shared server datastore and file/tool surfaces; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and largely inert.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write filesystem and uses browser and HTTP tools in flows, so attacker-controlled content can reach its prompts or tool nodes. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively inject, but if its content is copied into Flowise flows or files, the shared server datastore and file surfaces create a plausible injection path.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into a Flowise prompt, file, or tool node without sanitization
IF Flowise flows ingest uploaded files or browser output as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into prompts
Add a manual review step before importing content into Flowise
Use a strict delimiter/template for any copied reference text
Store imported snippets in read-only locations
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all flow inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and can read uploaded files, so it may expose user data if misconfigured. python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, network, or data classes touched, so it is not a leakage source. The pair’s leakage risk is limited because B is inert and A’s data class is only chatflow content.
conditions: IF sensitive data is uploaded into Flowise chatflows
IF Flowise outputs are copied into external systems
mitigations: Restrict uploads to non-sensitive test data
Turn off retention of chatflow artifacts where possible
Review Flowise logs for embedded secrets
Use separate credentials for test and production
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on flow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress, while python-cheatsheet has no write, network, or subprocess capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited to unusual deployment sharing rather than default contention.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator maps shared mutable state to both agents
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace
Mount python-cheatsheet read-only
Avoid shared git or database backends
Check deployment manifests for overlapping volumes
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise can produce outputs from graph-based flows, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and not runnable, so it cannot act on Flowise output. Any cascade is mainly manual: a person could copy Flowise output into the reference site or another workflow, which is weaker than the rubric’s default medium pathway.
conditions: IF a human treats Flowise output as authoritative and republishes it into another workflow
IF Flowise-generated text is copied into documentation without verification
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse of Flowise output
Label generated content as untrusted draft text
Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Add a checklist for source validation
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates in the Flowise flow

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated processing is evidenced. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and is documentation-only, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Flowise despite the current profiles
IF a deployment adds residency or retention requirements not present here
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair
Review deployment policy before enabling sensitive workflows
Keep secrets out of documentation-only content
Document data-class boundaries for operators
